solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: So narco's no source of illumination

parts.note: the word narco with its middle three letters taken away leaves the word no, so narco lightened by an arc is no

explanation.surface: A drug agent is said to be no bringer of light to anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction meaning 'lacking ARC'. Apply it to NARCO and NO is left, which is what the clue says.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc lamp produces brilliant light from an electric arc, so it is a lighting source used in film studios and searchlights.

clue.text: Positive this skilled tradesperson is biased

indicators.note: the clue says P set before the answer is a word meaning biased, so the answer is that word with P taken off

parts.note: partisan means one-sided, prejudiced in favour of a cause

explanation.surface: Someone claims a craftsman is prejudiced.
explanation.walkthrough: Put P (positive) in front of the answer and it becomes PARTISAN, meaning biased.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsperson working by hand at a trade, such as a carpenter or potter, is the standard sense of the word.

clue.text: Firm about communist beliefs

definitions.note: the answer is singular, a whole set of beliefs taken together

indicators.note: the letters for firm go around those for communist, which is what about signals

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
RED is the familiar term for a communist

explanation.surface: A company takes a stand on communist ideology.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed or statement of principles is a set of convictions, so the plural clue word fits the collective noun.

clue.text: At home on sofa I enjoyed being able to carry on eating

definitions.text: being able to carry on eating

parts.note: IN means at home
someone sitting on a sofa sat there
to have eaten something is to have enjoyed it, as in enjoying a meal

explanation.surface: Lounging at home on the sofa, someone admits to a meal they still want more of.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means never satisfied, so someone with this appetite could keep on consuming food.

clue.text: The wrong time of year unfortunately, so no radishes

indicators.note: things going unfortunately are going badly, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: It is the wrong season, sadly, so no radishes in the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase means out of season.
explanation.definitionFit: The French expression means out of season, the period when produce or activity is not usual.

clue.text: Queen caught felon breaking and entering 7A from the rear

indicators.note: entering means the scrambled felon letters go inside the other piece
from the rear means the piece is read backwards

parts.note: the figure 7 is written SEVEN, followed by the A as printed

indicators.note: breaking signals that the letters of felon, with C, are smashed into a new order

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A queen catches a burglar breaking and entering a house from the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking and entering' looks like the crime, but 'breaking' is an anagram sign and 'entering' a container sign; 7A is to be read as the number seven plus A, not a cross-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth wife of Henry VIII was a German princess who became Queen of England briefly in 1540.

clue.text: When visiting rellies, taking turn about remarkable Square

indicators.note: visiting means the word for when goes inside the relatives
taking a turn about means the relatives word is read backwards

parts.note: rellies is slang for relatives, kin
AS can mean when, as in as I left

explanation.surface: While staying with relatives, someone takes a stroll around a fine town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rellies' is Australian and British slang for relatives; a Nasik square is a magic square, which explains 'remarkable'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nasik square is a type of magic square with especially strong properties, named after the Indian city.

clue.text: Detailed twisted Christian harangue

indicators.note: twisted means turned about, so the surname is read backwards

parts.note: Christian Bale is the actor who played Batman
to harangue is to orate, lecture loudly

explanation.surface: A bent churchgoer lectures the congregation at length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christian' looks like a religious adjective but is the first name of the actor Christian Bale.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worked out with much intricacy and many parts is said to be complicated in that way.

clue.text: Motorsport director is given therapeutic toys

parts.note: F1, Formula One, written with the figure 1 read as the letter I
if something is given to you, you get it

explanation.surface: A racing team boss receives some stress-relief gadgets.
explanation.definitionFit: Small handheld gadgets such as spinners are sold to calm restless hands, an anxiety aid.

clue.text: Book about joining former volunteers is certainly light

indicators.note: joining means the word for about goes in among the volunteers

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, the old name for Britain's part-time reserve soldiers
RE means about, concerning
sure means certainly
to light is to land, as a bird lights on a branch

explanation.surface: A book on enlisting in the old army reserve is definitely lightweight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army was Britain's volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: The Robert Louis Stevenson novel of pirates and buried gold is a famous adventure title.

clue.text: See 9
Fodder one's gathered in for your old rat

indicators.note: gathered in means the letters for one's are held inside another piece

parts.note: TO and for are interchangeable in phrases like a present for her or to her
one's is read as one is, I'M
thy is the archaic form of your
to rat is to grass, inform on someone

explanation.surface: Someone stockpiles animal feed to deal with an elderly rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rat' looks like an animal but is the verb, and GRASS is British slang for informing.
explanation.definitionFit: A meadow plant grown widely as hay for livestock, so it is animal feed.

clue.text: Pud picked out by eye

parts.note: to pick something out by sight is to spot it
a private eye is a detective, called a dick in US slang

explanation.surface: A pudding is chosen just by looking at it.
explanation.walkthrough: SPOTTED DICK is a British steamed suet pudding with currants. 'by' is a link here, though spotted by a dick reads neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: A British steamed sponge dotted with dried fruit is a classic dessert, and pud is short for pudding.

clue.text: See 21
Sheepskin (or goatskin) apparently its source

indicators.note: the source of the answer is the run of letters lying across these words

explanation.surface: A leather is made from sheep, or possibly from goats.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft, supple leather from sheep or lambs, named after the Californian town Napa.

clue.text: Dotty storyteller collects homework after a break

indicators.note: collects means the storyteller holds the other piece inside

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the writer of tales
split homework into home and work: home is IN, work is TILL, as in tilling the soil

explanation.surface: A crazy narrator gathers up school work after the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a break' tells you to split 'homework' into two words, each replaced by a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes a pattern of tiny dots, as in decoration on bookbinding, so dotted.

clue.text: Try Morag perhaps with a drop of Glenmorangie in it?

definitions.text: Try Morag perhaps with a drop of Glenmorangie in it?

parts.note: to have a shot is to have a try

indicators.note: a drop of means only the first letter of the whisky name

parts.note: Morag is a Scottish girl's name, so an example of a lass

explanation.surface: Offer a Scottish girl a wee dram of a famous malt.
explanation.walkthrough: Glenmorangie is a Highland single malt whisky; the whole clue pictures what fills the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A small glass for a single measure of spirits, the kind used to hand someone a dram.

clue.text: Aged college dons close to retiring support singer

indicators.note: close to means only the final letter of the following word

parts.note: aged means old
C is an abbreviation for college; dons, putting on a hat, sets the letter from retiring on top in this down entry
a rest is a support, such as an armrest

explanation.surface: Elderly college dons near retirement help a choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like university teachers but is the verb: the last letter of 'retiring' goes on top of OLD and C.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny European songbird with a gold crown stripe, the singer here being a bird.

clue.text: Innocent man with his poached fish skewers

indicators.note: man skewers the fish, so the letters for fish sit inside the man

parts.note: taken as written
the ide is a freshwater fish, also called orfe

indicators.note: poached means cooked, so the word his is cooked into a new order

explanation.surface: A man with his poached fish spears it on kebab sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Like a young unmarried girl, so naive and untouched, describing someone innocent.

clue.text: Deer in bits OK, escaping horse and donkey

indicators.note: in bits means the two letters are separate, not a single run
escaping means these letters leave the other words

parts.note: a mount is a horse you ride
a jack is a male donkey
taken as written

explanation.surface: A deer survives, smashed but fine, after a horse and a donkey get away.
explanation.walkthrough: The O leaves MOUNT and the K leaves JACK.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Asian deer, also called the barking deer, now feral in English woodland.

clue.text: Blyton's second, in periodical instalments: Five Stood Still at Sea

indicators.note: second means the second letter of the author's name
taking letters at regular intervals gives every other one

explanation.surface: An Enid Blyton serial issues another Five adventure title about being becalmed.
explanation.walkthrough: Enid Blyton wrote the Famous Five books. Alternate letters of 'Five Stood' give IETO.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing term for a ship brought to a halt with its head to the wind, so motionless on the water.

clue.text: Ultimately Famous Five are muddled in head, see

indicators.note: the two letters swap places within the coin side, which is what muddled in signals

parts.note: the obverse is the heads side of a coin

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of the next word

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: In the end the Famous Five get confused in the head, you see.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of 'Famous' (S) and 'Five' (V) swap places in OBVERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch or notice something is to perceive it with the eyes.

clue.text: Zip lacking elasticity

parts.note: lacking means having no
muscle tone is firmness and springiness

explanation.surface: A zip fastener that has lost its stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Zip is slang for nothing at all, as in zero, and the phrase means none whatsoever.

clue.text: Honour bestowed for one courageous check on autopilot

indicators.note: on means the check comes after the autopilot in this across entry

parts.note: George is pilots' slang for the automatic pilot
to cross is to check or thwart

explanation.surface: A bravery medal is awarded after a flight controls test.
explanation.walkthrough: The George Cross is Britain's highest civilian award for gallantry.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest British civilian gallantry award, given for acts of great bravery.

clue.text: Had to carry grain jar

indicators.note: in a down entry, the meal word carries the grain on its back, so it sits below

parts.note: GR is the abbreviation for grain, the weight unit
to have a meal is to eat it, so had means ate

explanation.surface: Someone had to carry a jar of grain.
explanation.definitionFit: To grate on someone is to irritate, as a jarring sound does.

clue.text: Senior ex-army man?

indicators.note: ex means out of, so these letters come out

parts.note: a soldier is an army man

explanation.surface: An elderly veteran soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: an old former soldier is a senior.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for an elderly person, here one who was once in the army.

clue.text: Time system Canada learns about, losing a second on Canada Day

indicators.note: on means the date comes first, with the rest following in this across entry

parts.note: Canada Day falls on 1 July, written JUL 1 with the figure read as I

indicators.note: about signals the remaining letters are rearranged
losing means these letters drop out of the fodder

explanation.surface: A dating method Canadians study, missing a moment on their national day.
explanation.definitionFit: The dating scheme introduced by Julius Caesar, replaced by the Gregorian one, is a way of reckoning years.

clue.text: See 24
See 5
Somehow, sex used to be on a rota before

indicators.note: on a rota means taking turns, so the letters move round from one end to the other

parts.note: IT is slang for sex appeal or sex
was means used to be
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Sex was a scheduled duty in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a rota' moves ITW from the front to the back of ITWAS, giving ASITW.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in a way, so to speak, hedging what one says.
